- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3–5% above recent peak for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.3) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast to avoid premature mean reversion.
- Model frequently underestimates true price in early forecast window (e.g., day 1–5 of 30d); apply +1–2% bias to first 5 days if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.
- If sentiment history shows repeated low values (e.g., 0.00–0.30) over 3+ days, model tends to lag; forecast should be adjusted upward by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.3–0.7), model often fails to capture mean reversion; use 3-day moving average of true prices as baseline for correction.
- For long-term forecasts (day 15–30), model tends to underestimate if sentiment is weak; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast if sentiment <0.4 over last 5 days.
- If model forecast is consistently higher than true outcome by >2% for 3+ consecutive days, reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period unless sentiment is strong.
